UX projects and concepts

Earlier UX work and ongoing concepts, each shaped through research, testing and iteration.

TUH for All

Redesign of the Thammasat University Hospital patient app

Most of the app's users are older patients, many with presbyopia or myopia, and the dense menus and small tap targets made it hard for them to use. I reorganized the app around one main task per screen, enlarged the touch targets, and put the patient's name, HN number and photo right after login so they can see they're in the right account.

Users
Older patients, the majority of TUH's users
Method
Usability testing and interviews, which gave more direct feedback from older users than a survey would
Principles
Larger type, high contrast, one action per screen, identity always visible, an easy way back home
Open in Figma

ZenTime

Capstone project · Time-management app · React Native

Designed for Pang, a 32-year-old office worker whose to-do app had “more features than necessary.” ZenTime keeps only the essentials: tasks are prioritized with the Eisenhower matrix, the UI uses a warm monochrome palette in a 60-30-10 ratio, and the app runs on React Native with offline SQLite storage.

Research
Persona and pain-point interviews; tested with 6 users aged 19–33
Stack
React Native, SQLite (offline-first), Figma prototyping
Finding
Creating and reviewing tasks went smoothly. Deleting items and a few unclear icons caused friction, both fixed in the next iteration
Open in Figma

Chicken Ready ฟาร์มไก่พร้อม

Field research · Farm-management app for small poultry farmers

Visits to small chicken farms showed that inconsistent record-keeping was eating into already thin margins. I designed a step-by-step flow for logging flock size, feed costs and other expenses, simple enough for owners who rarely use apps.

Users
Small-scale chicken farmers, many using an app for the first time
Goal
Track income and expenses, with hygiene guidance in the same place
Approach
Step-by-step forms instead of dashboards, one number at a time
Open in Figma

Farm ฟาร์ม

Concept · Gamified attendance app to reduce lateness at work

A side project for my own workplace. Each on-time check-in tills, plants and grows a small farm plot: arriving on time waters and fertilizes the crops, while lateness or absence lets them dry out. A streak bonus (×1.5 after 12 days) rewards consistency, and harvested crops can be sold for coins in an in-app shop.

Users
Employees at my company, building a daily check-in habit
Mechanic
Till → plant → water → fertilize → harvest, tied to attendance status, with a streak bonus and an in-app shop
Status
Figma concept in progress, mapping the full loop before planning the build
Open in Figma

Social media graphics

Monthly promotion posts for Time To Fitness, designed as one campaign so the series reads as a set in the feed.

October Mission Time To Fitness

A month-long sale: one key visual announcing up to 30% off, followed by nine product posts. Every post reuses the same system — a red-and-white showroom set, a bold price lockup, a free-gift tag and the campaign mark — so each one works alone and the series still holds together.

Client
Time To Fitness
Format
10 square social posts, 1:1
Campaign
October 2026 monthly promotion

Design, with a CS background

I'm Poh, a UX/UI designer with a Computer Science degree from Thammasat University. I work across design and front-end code, so I care about two things equally: whether an older patient can find the home button, and whether the layout actually holds up in the browser.

Before design, I worked as a choreographer and assistant stylist on GMM TV productions, and on event staff at concerts and book fairs around Bangkok. Stage work taught me a lot about timing and guiding where people look, and I still use that every day.

Right now I focus on redesigning websites for sports and fitness retail brands, while continuing research-based UX work: personas, usability testing and design systems that are ready to hand off.
